name: Trump Taj Mahal

summary.text: The Trump Taj Mahal was an Atlantic City casino that opened in April 1990, financed with about $675 million of junk bonds, and entered a prepackaged Chapter 11 in 1991 that gave bondholders half its equity. In 1998 FinCEN penalized Trump Taj Mahal Associates for currency transaction reporting violations. On March 6, 2015 FinCEN announced a $10 million civil money penalty against the casino for willful and repeated Bank Secrecy Act violations in 2010-2012, noting that examiners had cited BSA violations at the casino going back to 2003; the casino's parent, Trump Entertainment Resorts, was then in its 2014 Chapter 11 case, from which it emerged in February 2016 as a subsidiary of Carl Icahn's Icahn Enterprises. The Taj Mahal closed on October 10, 2016.

facts.claim: On March 6, 2015 FinCEN announced a $10 million civil money penalty against Trump Taj Mahal Casino Resort for willful and repeated violations of the Bank Secrecy Act; the casino admitted it lacked an effective anti-money-laundering program, failed to report suspicious transactions, filed currency transaction reports improperly and kept inadequate records.
facts.quote: The casino admitted it lacked an effective anti-money-laundering program, did not report suspicious transactions, filed required currency transaction reports improperly, and kept inadequate records

In the Matter of Trump Taj Mahal Casino Resort

facts.claim: FinCEN's assessment found the casino willfully violated the BSA's program, reporting and recordkeeping requirements from 2010 through 2012, and stated that many of the violations had previously been flagged by IRS examinations of the casino going back to 2003.
facts.quote: many of these violations had previously been flagged by IRS SB/SE in examinations of the casino going back to 2003

facts.claim: As part of the 2015 action the casino must have periodic external audits of its anti-money-laundering compliance program, with reports going to FinCEN and to its board of directors.
facts.quote: the casino must have periodic external audits of its AML compliance program, with reports going to FinCEN and its Board of Directors

facts.claim: FinCEN's 2015 release recalled that in 1998 the Trump Taj Mahal had paid a $477,700 civil money penalty for currency transaction reporting violations; FinCEN's 1998 announcement concerned failures to file currency transaction reports between April 1990 and December 1991 following an IRS examination, and gave the figure as $477,000.
facts.quote: FinCEN's 1998 announcement covered failures to file currency transaction reports for violations from April 1990 through December 1991, and it was tied to an IRS examination. The penalty amount announced was $477,000.

facts.claim: The 2015 penalty was agreed while the casino's parent was in Chapter 11; the bankruptcy court approved the settlement on March 4, 2015, and a bankruptcy filing disclosed that FinCEN imposed the penalty on January 27, 2015. FinCEN's assessment noted the parent had filed for Chapter 11 three times since 2004.
facts.quote: The casino's parent entity had also filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection three times since 2004, emerging from its first bankruptcy in May 2005 and re-entering in February 2009. The 2015 settlement was approved by the bankruptcy court on March 4, 2015.

facts.claim: In November 1990, after missing a $47.25 million bond payment, Trump agreed to a prepackaged Chapter 11 plan for the Taj Mahal under which holders of the casino's $675 million junk-bond issue would receive half its equity, bond maturity was extended from 1998 to 2000, and Trump remained chairman and appointed a majority of the board.
facts.quote: The 'pre-packaged Chapter 11 plan' would prevent the deal from being derailed by dissenting bondholders, who he said might try to force the issue of the default by filing for involuntary bankruptcy.

sources.title: Trump's Taj Mahal casino to enter 'consensual' bankruptcy

facts.claim: Trump Entertainment Resorts filed for Chapter 11 on September 9, 2014 and said it would close the Taj Mahal in November unless it obtained concessions from its unions; its sister casino, Trump Plaza, closed permanently on September 16, 2014.
facts.quote: Trump Entertainment Resorts filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on September 9, 2014, and announced plans to close the Taj Mahal on November 13 if the casino did not get concessions from its unions.

sources.title: Trump Entertainment Resorts files for bankruptcy

facts.claim: Trump Entertainment Resorts emerged from bankruptcy on February 26, 2016 as a subsidiary of Carl Icahn's Icahn Enterprises LP; Bloomberg reported that Donald Trump had not been involved in managing the casino since its most recent bankruptcy.
facts.quote: Trump Entertainment Resorts Inc., the casino operator founded by Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump, emerged from bankruptcy court protection on Friday and is now a subsidiary of billionaire Carl Icahn's Icahn Enterprises LP.

facts.claim: In August 2016 the company announced the Taj Mahal would close after Labor Day; it closed on October 10, 2016 after failing to reach a contract with union workers, with about 3,000 jobs lost.
facts.quote: Atlantic City's Trump Taj Mahal casino and hotel will close its doors permanently after Labor Day, less than seven months after the establishment exited bankruptcy as a subsidiary of billionaire investor Carl Icahn.

openQuestions: The 1998 penalty figure differs between FinCEN's 1998 release ($477,000) and its 2015 release ($477,700); the 1998 assessment document should settle it.
The 1991 plan terms are taken from UPI's November 1990 report of the agreement; the court-confirmed 1991 plan was not reached.
Icahn's December 2014 $20 million financing commitment was only seen in a reference site and was left out.
